identity.name: Potassium carbonates
identity.chemical_class: Inorganic alkaline potassium salts of carbonic acid

function.mechanism: Carbonate and bicarbonate neutralize acids and buffer pH; bicarbonate can release carbon dioxide under acidic/thermal conditions, supporting leavening.

adi.basis: No dedicated EFSA E501 food-additive ADI was identified in accessible EFSA sources during this research run.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA call-for-data documentation lists E501(i) and E501(ii) among permitted EU additives in re-evaluation preparation, but no dedicated published EFSA E501 food-additive opinion was identified in the accessible sources searched here.

fda.notes: Both sections state use in food with no limitation other than current good manufacturing practice and list functional use conditions.

adi.basis: ADI not limited for potassium carbonate (INS 501(i)) and potassium hydrogen carbonate (INS 501(ii)).

concerns.summary: Physiologic potassium-load risk can increase in people with impaired potassium excretion (e.g., chronic kidney disease) or with medications that reduce potassium excretion; hyperkalemia risk is context-dependent rather than specific to a low additive ADI threshold.

Recent PubMed results contain limited direct E501 food-additive safety studies; available newer studies are mostly supplementation or experimental-model studies (including a mouse acidosis model with potassium bicarbonate).

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA assigned ADI 'not limited' for INS 501(i) and INS 501(ii).
U.S. CFR sections 21 CFR 184.1619 and 21 CFR 184.1613 affirm GRAS use under GMP conditions.

populations: people with chronic kidney disease or reduced urinary potassium excretion
people using ACE inhibitors or potassium-sparing diuretics
adi_exceedance.notes: JECFA uses 'ADI not limited' for E501 components, so conventional ADI exceedance is not the primary issue; risk is linked to total potassium handling capacity in susceptible populations.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators continue to permit E501 with GMP controls, and JECFA classifies both components as ADI not limited. The main concern is potassium-load susceptibility in vulnerable populations rather than broad hazard at typical general-population additive exposure.
key_factors: JECFA ADI not limited for INS 501(i) and 501(ii)
FDA GRAS status in 21 CFR 184.1619 and 184.1613 under GMP
Vulnerable-population hyperkalemia risk from total potassium burden
